title: Buildings the City rents that changed hands after the lease
question: Did the owners of buildings the City rents sell after the City signed, so that the lease went with the building to a new owner?
finding: 14 rented sites show a sale date after the City's first lease file (2018 on) or a value re-set on the 2026-27 roll with no date. 6 of the sales are new to the record from the hand-saved rolls: 752 Vallejo Street (31 March 2026, 1,421 days after the lease file of 10 May 2022); 333 Valencia Street; 333 Valencia (3 February 2026, 2,058 days after the lease file of 16 June 2020); 2000 Oakdale Avenue (2 January 2026, 3,559 days after the lease file of 5 April 2016); 141 Industrial Street; 141 Industrial (22 April 2026, 701 days after the lease file of 21 May 2024); 760 Harrison Street (1 April 2024, 3,289 days after the lease file of 31 March 2015); 3801 Third Street (4 October 2023, 1,443 days after the lease file of 22 October 2019). 1380 Howard Street: value $5,397,142 on the 2025-26 roll and $28,298,880 on the 2026-27 roll with no sale date.
how: Every Board file with the City as tenant that the parcels screen matched to a parcel. A sale date on any roll (portal 2007-2025 or the nine workbooks) after the first lease file and from 2018 on is listed; so is a value that rose more than one and a half times and by over $1 million between the 2025-26 and 2026-27 rolls. Landlord names and rents are as the parcels screen already read them from the Board file titles (individuals are not named).
limits: A building with a long-term tenant is an ordinary thing to sell, and a lease normally binds the buyer. A sale date may also record a refinancing, a transfer between related companies or the sale of a share. The rolls give no owner and no price. What would settle it: the deed and transfer-tax declaration (Assessor-Recorder) and the Real Estate Division's file on whether the lease was assigned or renegotiated, and at what rent. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
